previous_issues.note: R13 queries open episodes by team, episode department, bucket and optional `ownerConsoleUserId`, sorts on `since`, paginates on episodes, then joins; two indexes named; the badge counts the same query; A5 and A13 cite R13. Residual: the episode field list in R12 has no team field for the R13 index to use (new r3-1).

Key is lead + department across channels; unique partial index where open; duplicate-key insert a silent no-op; mutable `unanswered_episodes` split from append-only `unanswered_episode_transitions`; writers named (shared service, sweeper, R4 endpoint). Field types are still not given; not blocking. How aging interacts with the 'where open' index is undefined (new r3-2).

R5 claims the summary with a unique upsert on recipient + department + window before sending; later escalations go at window end; retry, `text_failed`, `textAttempts`, `lastTextError` and episode ids sit on the summary; A24 and A28 test it. The summary record's collection is unnamed; minor, not raised.
R4: open queues a deduped refresh (lead + department), inbound never waits, stored owner shows meanwhile; R2 routes CRM activity through the R4 endpoint; A22 covers slow, down or failing reads.

R1 names SMS `authorType: HUMAN`, states email and chat have no member send; R12 backfills only where replies are observable (SMS `authorType`, claim and release events, action item creation and completion), the rest labelled.
Allowlist is explicit normalised intents written at enablement; new ones open nothing until added; A2 adds the unlisted case.

issues.quote: Indexes: team + department + status + `since`, and with `ownerConsoleUserId`.
issues.concern: The index leads on team, but the R12 field list for `unanswered_episodes` (`leadId`, `department`, `status`, `since`, `channel`, `reason`, `ownerConsoleUserId`, ...) has no team or enterprise field. Without it, R13 has to go back through `leads` to filter by team, which is the lead pre-query R13 exists to avoid, and the index cannot be built as written.
issues.because: R12 field list vs R13 index; `conversational-ai-backend:src/customers/customers.service.ts:2452` (team list scopes by enterprise and team through leads today)
issues.ask: Add `enterpriseId` and `teamId` to the episode document, set at open from the lead and never changed, and lead the R13 indexes with them. Ten minutes of spec work; fold it into the build ticket.

issues.quote: an episode past its aging cutoff on the R5 in-hours clock moves to the aged bucket: off the badge, in R7, unreplied in metrics.
issues.concern: The status that 'aged' sets is undefined, and the unique partial index is 'where open'. If aged stays `open`, a customer who texts again on Monday joins the aged episode and stays off the badge: the be-back nobody sees, which is the failure this feature exists to remove. If aged sets another status, the new text opens a second episode for the same lead + department, and the old one sits in R7 forever unless a reply clears both.
issues.because: R3, R12 (partial index where open), A16; E10, E13
issues.ask: Define `status` values (open, aged, cleared) and the index predicate. State that a new human-owed customer message on an aged episode moves it back to active with a new `since` (or closes it as aged and opens a fresh one), and that a reply clears every uncleared episode for lead + department. AC: episode aged Friday, customer texts Monday in hours, it is on the badge.

issues.quote: A clear matches the `episodeId` it read.
issues.concern: Only the click clear reads an episode id. A console reply and a CRM activity clear arriving through the R4 endpoint carry a lead, a department and a time, not an episode id. Matching on an id they do not have either drops those clears or invents a lookup that races with a new open.
issues.because: R2 (reply and CRM activity clears), R4 endpoint
issues.ask: Say: click clears match `episodeId`; reply and CRM activity clears match lead + department with `since` before the activity time, so activity older than a newly opened episode never clears it.

issues.quote: Ship the unique index before the writer switch?
issues.concern: This is not open. A unique index cannot be built over a collection that already holds duplicate open rows, and R12's atomic open depends on it. If the writer runs first, Phase 0 data can block the index.
issues.ask: Close Open question 8: the indexes ship in the deploy before the writer switch turns on, and the writer stays off if the unique index is missing.
